observations: Photo 0 shows a stack of used wooden pallets with white labels and one pallet lying flat on dirt ground.
Photo 1 shows a similar stack of wooden pallets from a slightly different angle with a truck and cars in the background.
Photo 2 shows wooden pallets with oval EPAL stamps visible on corner blocks, stacked under a covered shed.
Photo 3 shows a close-up side view of a wooden pallet or crate panel held upright by a person.

claims.evidence: photos 0-3 show wooden slats, blocks, and fasteners
EPAL stamps in photo 2 suggest European origin but import status cannot be confirmed from photos alone

risks.risk: Broken, cracked, or rotten slats and blocks hidden in the stack
risks.proof: close-up video or photos of each pallet's deck boards, stringers, and blocks
wide shot of the entire lot with a visible count, or an itemized quantity from the seller

risks.risk: Missing heat treatment or ISPM 15 stamps required for imported wood packaging
risks.proof: close-up photos of IPPC/HT stamps on pallet blocks

risks.risk: Contamination from chemical spills or cargo residue
risks.proof: close-up inspection of deck boards and stringers for stains or odors

proof_requests: Wide shot showing the full stack and total pallet count
Close-up photos of EPAL and IPPC/HT stamps on multiple pallets
Close-up video of pallet undersides and stringers to check for breaks or rot
response.reason: The item is identifiable as used wooden pallets from the photos, so a worst-case price per pallet as damaged scrap can be set despite unverified origin and hidden condition risks.
